t: You're on Lavender Hill, a hill and street in Battersea. Two people were born here. Catherine Gurney, who lived from 1848 to 1930, was a British temperance activist. She is remembered for setting up police convalescent homes, orphanages and schools, and the charity she founded, the Gurney Fund, still exists. Sidney Knights, who lived from 1898 to 1968, was an English flying ace in the First World War, credited with eight aerial victories.
